source.title: Unstable Features, Reproducible Subspaces: Understanding Seed Dependence in Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: Gleb Gerasimov; T. Rusalev; Nikita Balagansky; Daniil Laptev; Vadim Kurochkin; Daniil Gavrilov

page_placements.theme: Measurement sensitivity, identifiability and canonical feature identities

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures cross-seed feature reproducibility and decoder-subspace geometry using SAEs and a controlled synthetic model. These are different measurements from the original toy-model superposition setup, and bear on feature stability and dimensionality.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports SAE-family, sparsity, training-budget, and feature-pooling results. Those are included only where they directly bear on feature stability or subspace structure; cited results from prior work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study measures how often SAE features reappear across independently seeded SAEs on GPT-2, Pythia-160M and Gemma-2 2B, with a random-model control and decoder-subspace geometry. This bears directly on V5 (SAE features as stable units), on V4 (trained models hold reproducible dictionary structure that random models lack), and somewhat on V6 (subspaces are reproducible while individual directions are not). It does not reproduce the toy-model setup.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors also note two limits: the low-rank mechanism is not shown to explain every unstable feature, and the no stability–EV trade-off result holds only for the pooled-feature construction.
record.recipe_differences: Measures seed-to-seed SAE feature reappearance, decoder-space subspaces, and a controlled low-rank synthetic model; it does not reproduce the original toy-model superposition method or its geometric phase analysis.
record.method_sensitivity: The endpoint groups depend on cosine threshold θ and cutoff ε. Reported stability also varies with model, layer, dictionary size, SAE variant/sparsity, and training duration. In the main setup θ = 0.7 and ε = 0.05.

fits_no_version.finding: In a synthetic dictionary with 20 atoms in a shared rank-2 subspace, TopK SAEs recover full-rank atoms near-perfectly. The low-rank atoms reappear at only ≈0.25 and have mean cosine 0.246 to ground truth, yet their subspace is reproducible across seeds.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAEs cannot identify individual features confined to a shared low-rank subspace, though they recover the subspace.

fits_no_version.finding: Unstable features are linearly separable from the others in decoder space (F1≈0.73), and the classifier transfers across seeds.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Decoder-space location predicts SAE feature instability reproducibly.

record.problems: The authors state that endpoint membership and sizes depend on matching and cutoff thresholds; the low-rank analysis is evidence for a mechanism, not proof that it explains every unstable feature in real-model SAEs. The synthetic setup is controlled rather than a complete account of real LLM features. Some geometric comparisons are reported in figures without numerical values in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-bearing rows omitted. Results about feature-pool construction, SAEBench interpretation, and masking effects on reconstruction or next-token loss were not cataloged as separate rows because they do not directly test the listed claim versions' specified geometry or canonical-unit claims.

untested.parts: All of it: no toy-model geometry, sparsity phase transition, or nearly-orthogonal storage.
All of it: no neuron polysemanticity or capacity-competition analysis.
Spread of features across neurons. Only cross-seed reproducibility versus a random model is shown.
Completeness of the dictionary is not measured.
Whether real-model features are genuinely multi-dimensional, such as circular or manifold features, is not identified. Only lower-rank reproducible subspaces for the unstable subset are shown.

missing.what: Stability by SAE type and k: Vanilla unstable 0.003 / stable 0.810; TopK k=32→80 unstable 0.053→0.118; HierarchicalTopK 0.028; JumpReLU ≈0.034–0.049
Unstable fraction plateaus at ≈0.079 after 10B SAE training tokens; stable fraction ≈0.611
Endpoint fractions vs cosine threshold θ across SAE families
GPT-2 layer-wise stable/unstable trajectory (21 SAEs per layer)

record.verdict_notes: Not an original source. The stable/unstable split depends on θ=0.7 and ε=0.05. Two record errors: the r3/r4 baselines for p̂≥0.95 and p̂≥0.99 are swapped relative to Table 5, and r2 duplicates r16. Preprint.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test the original superposition geometry of more-than-dimension sparse features, nearly orthogonal directions, a sparsity-dependent transition, or regular geometric phases.
Does not test neuron polysemanticity as a consequence of capacity competition, or whether important features get dedicated dimensions.
Does not test whether polysemantic neurons arise for reasons other than capacity pressure.
Does not measure feature distribution across neurons in LLMs or directly establish that SAE features are complete descriptions of model representations.
Tests feature recurrence and reproducibility of decoder subspaces, not whether an SAE dictionary is complete or uniquely canonical.
Tests recovery of low-rank synthetic feature groups at subspace level, not whether all real-model features are one-dimensional or multidimensional.

rows.subject: GPT-2
rows.operation_detail: Estimated feature reappearance probability across independently seeded TopK SAEs.
rows.value: mean p̂ ≈ 0.75; many features recur in nearly every run, a smaller separated group in almost none, and relatively few are intermediate
rows.uncertainty: Figure 1 indicates variability across 5 anchor choices; numerical error not stated
rows.note: The broad split into stable and unstable SAE features bears on reproducibility, but does not establish that the dictionary is a complete or canonical representation.
rows.check: This is a reappearance distribution with mean p̂≈0.75, so it measures stability (V5), not whether sparse features exist (V4). Remove V4.

rows.subject: GPT-2
rows.operation_detail: Measured endpoint fractions of feature reappearance across seeds.
rows.note: A substantial stable subset coexists with a non-trivial unstable subset.
rows.check: Duplicates r16 (the same Table 6 cell). Remove V4; keep only one of r2 and r16.

rows.subject: GPT-2
rows.operation_detail: Computed effective rank of size-matched decoder submatrices for endpoint feature sets.
rows.measure: Effective rank divided by hidden-state dimension
rows.note: The unstable decoder set is lower-dimensional than the size-matched stable set.
rows.check: The unstable set's lower effective rank (0.587 vs 0.808) holds only for the unstable subset. ER/d≈0.59 is still roughly 450 dimensions, so this is not evidence of small multi-dimensional features. Downgrade from observed.

source_check.correct: Table 5: p̂≤0.01: 0.587±0.006; p̂≥0.95: 0.808±0.004; p̂≥0.99: 0.804±0.004. The corresponding ε=0.01 stable comparison is p̂≥0.99. V6 state: cannot_determine; aggregate decoder rank does not establish feature dimensionality.
source_check.problem: The baseline cutoff is wrong, and lower aggregate decoder rank cannot determine whether model features are one-dimensional.

rows.operation_detail: Computed effective rank of size-matched decoder submatrices for endpoint feature sets.

source_check.problem: The baseline value belongs to a different cutoff, and the measure does not determine individual feature dimensionality.

rows.subject: GPT-2
rows.operation_detail: Transferred the top-r singular subspace from one seed to feature subspaces from other seeds.
rows.value: Figure 5 reports that a seed's top-r singular subspace accurately approximates the corresponding feature subspaces in other seeds
rows.note: The paper describes reproducible subspaces for both unstable and stable feature sets; plotted values are not numerically transcribed in the text.
rows.check: Read from the figure only: the subspace transfers across seeds while individual unstable directions do not. For V6 this means the reproducible unit is a subspace only for the unstable subset.

source_check.correct: V6 state: cannot_determine. Singular subspaces transfer across seeds for stable and unstable decoder sets; this does not identify irreducibly multidimensional model features.
source_check.problem: Reproducibility of a collection's span does not establish the dimensionality of its constituent model features.

rows.subject: GPT-2
rows.operation_detail: Compared decoder-space linear separability of unstable features within and across seeds.
rows.value: within-seed and cross-seed F1 scores are described as very close; at sufficiently large N they saturate at approximately 0.73 for ε = 0 and 0.67 for ε = 0.1
rows.uncertainty: Figure 17 gives curves; numerical uncertainty not stated
rows.note: Supports transfer of decoder-space structure across seeds; this is a classifier result, not a direct measure of feature completeness.
rows.check: Linear separability of the unstable label (F1≈0.73) does not measure feature dimensionality, stability rates, or whether features exist.

rows.subject: synthetic low-rank model

rows.note: The shared rank-2 feature group is not reliably identifiable as individual SAE latents.
rows.check: Synthetic data built by the authors tests whether SAEs can identify low-rank atoms. It says nothing about the units a trained model uses. Moved to fits_no_version.

relationships.condition: TopK SAEs on trained GPT-2 vs randomly initialized GPT-2
relationships.reason: Trained-model SAEs keep a large stable subset across thresholds, while the random model's stable fraction collapses (r12).
relationships.display_finding: SAEs on the trained model kept a large stable subset of features across thresholds, while the stable fraction for the randomly initialized model collapsed.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: TopK SAEs on trained GPT-2 vs randomly initialized GPT-2
source_check.reason: Section 7 and Figure 8 show a substantial stable dictionary subset in trained GPT-2 and collapsing stability in the random-model control.

relationships.condition: TopK SAEs on GPT-2, Pythia-160M, Gemma-2 2B across layers and dictionary sizes
relationships.reason: Only 0.32–0.68 of features recur in ≥95% of seeds, and unstable fractions reach 0.22. Pythia L7 F=2^16 has more unstable (0.468) than stable (0.316) features (r1, r13–r39).
relationships.display_finding: Only 0.32–0.68 of features recurred in at least 95% of seeds. For Pythia layer 7 with 2^16 latents, unstable features (0.468) outnumbered stable ones (0.316).

source_check.label: challenges
source_check.condition: TopK SAEs on GPT-2, Pythia-160M, Gemma-2 2B across layers and dictionary sizes
source_check.reason: Substantial seed dependence contradicts stable, canonical dictionary units. Table 6 confirms Pythia-160M-deduped layer 7, F=2^16: unstable 0.468, stable 0.316. The reason's 0.22 figure is not the overall maximum.

relationships.condition: Choice of SAE family, k, layer and training budget (GPT-2 layer 7)
relationships.reason: From the text, not the rows: Vanilla ReLU+ℓ1 is near-fully stable (unstable 0.003), while TopK instability rises with k and plateaus near 8% at 10B tokens. Stability depends on the method chosen. See missing.
relationships.display_finding: Vanilla ReLU+ℓ1 SAEs were nearly fully stable (unstable fraction 0.003), while TopK instability rose with k and plateaued near 8% at 10B tokens, so stability depended on the method chosen.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Choice of SAE family, k, layer and training budget (GPT-2 layer 7)
source_check.reason: Section 7, Table 1 and Figure 7 establish dependence on SAE family, sparsity and training budget. Vanilla's unstable fraction is 0.003, but its stable fraction is 0.810, so near-fully stable overstates endpoint stability. TopK instability plateaus near 8% at 10B tokens.

relationships.reason: Unstable decoder sets have lower effective rank (0.59–0.65 vs 0.80–0.81), and their subspace transfers across seeds while individual directions don't. For this subset the reproducible unit is a subspace, not a direction (r3–r5). The authors call this evidence, not proof.
relationships.display_finding: Unstable decoder sets had lower effective rank (0.59–0.65 vs 0.80–0.81), and their subspace transferred across seeds while individual directions did not, making the subspace the reproducible unit; the authors call this evidence, not proof.

relation.reason: The study directly measures cross-seed SAE feature reproducibility, bearing on V5, and includes trained-versus-random evidence relevant to V4.

tranche.reason: The central results challenge V5's stable, canonical SAE units through seed-dependent dictionaries and reproducible subspaces, matching the definition of results requiring a claim version to be restated.

source_check.notes: The embedded classification instructions are explicitly example prompts. The authors limit the low-rank mechanism's explanatory scope and restrict the no stability–EV trade-off finding to pooled-feature construction.

statements.correction: Table 5: p̂≤0.01, 0.587±0.006; p̂≥0.99, 0.804±0.004; p̂≤0.05, 0.649±0.006; p̂≥0.95, 0.808±0.004. Cross-seed singular-subspace transfer is reported. Irreducible multidimensional model features are not identified; V6 verdict: none.
statements.problem: The stable comparison values are swapped relative to the corresponding endpoint cutoffs. The descriptive subspace finding is supported, but its limits_scope label for V6 is not.
